extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents and IP practitioners handling Indian patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and maintaining disclosures and documentary responses required under Section 8 of the Indian Patents Act (including Form 3 and responses to Controller requests) when prosecuting Indian patent applications that have corresponding foreign filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Section 8(1) / Form 3 (detailed particulars of corresponding applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant is prosecuting an application for a patent in any country outside India in respect of the same or substantially the same invention, he shall file ... a statement setting out detailed particulars of such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entering national phase (PCT or Paris Convention) or where corresponding foreign applications exist, disclose details of such foreign applications by filing Form 3 included in the Patent schedule. Disclosure of the foreign application itself (application number, filing date, jurisdictions, status etc.) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing Form 3 (Section 8(1) timing and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement under Section 8(1) must be filed 'along with his application or subsequently within the prescribed period as the Controller may allow'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not disclosed at filing, the common practice is to file Form 3 within six months from the filing date in India. That six-month period may be extended by one month upon filing a request for extension of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undertaking to update Controller up to grant (Section 8(1)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must give an undertaking that, up to the date of grant of patent in India, he would keep the Controller informed in writing, from time to time, of detailed particulars as required under clause (a) in respect of every other application relating to the same or substantially the same invention filed subsequently outside India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation continues until grant; particulars of subsequently filed corresponding foreign applications should be furnished within the prescribed time (typically six months from filing in the respective country).

rubrics_metrics.name: Which foreign applications count as 'same or substantially same'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patents Act / Rules do not specifically define 'same or substantially same inventions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, consider Paris Convention/PCT national stage family members, applications sharing a common priority date, continuation applications, divisional applications, and continuation-in-part applications as corresponding applications for disclosure purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller practice variability and discretionary interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Controllers differ in approach: some take a rigid stand interpreting the prescribed period as discretionary, while others allow filing Form 3 within six months of the Indian filing irrespective of when corresponding foreign apps were filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of divergent Controller practices; agents should be prepared to present reasoned arguments and contest objections based on reasonable interpretations of the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late filing consequences and remedy (irregularity / petition u/r 137)
rubrics_metrics.description: If details of existing foreign applications are furnished within six months of filing the Indian application but were filed prior to the Indian filing, some Controllers may consider this an irregularity and may raise an objection in the First Examination Report (FER) or during hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To overcome such objection, file a petition under Rule 137 requesting condonation/obviation of the irregularity. Although uncommon, this practice has occurred and may be monetary- or procedure-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of status updates (whether to update Form 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants often include status updates (filed, pending, issued, examination report issued, etc.) for corresponding foreign applications, but the Patents Act only requires disclosure of the foreign application itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Controllers do not require continuous status updates; however, Exception 1 notes some Controllers interpret that any change in status of a corresponding foreign application must be updated through Form 3 within six months of such update — failure may invite objection and require petition under Rule 137. Consider updating where strategic or where interacting Controller has such expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO / validation-related practice (Exception for EP filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files an application with the EPO, they may later validate the EP in designated states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally Controllers do not consider it irregular if the EP application details were disclosed within prescribed time even if later validations in designated states are not separately disclosed. However, some Controllers may ask for information on validations within six months of their respective validations and may treat non-disclosure as irregularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller-invoked requirement under Section 8(2) (documents relating to processing abroad)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after an application is filed in India and till grant or refusal, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish details relating to the processing of the application in a country outside India, and the applicant shall furnish information available to him within such period as may be prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical documents requested under Section 8(2) include search and examination reports, office actions, notices of allowance, grant or refusal decisions, and granted/allowed claims. These must be provided in English where originally in a foreign language. The obligation under 8(2) arises on Controller request (not automatically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and practical filing of Section 8(2) documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 8(2) documents need not be voluntarily submitted but are typically filed within six months upon invitation by the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common practice is to file Section 8(2) documents along with the response to the FER within six months of the FER date, or within the first month of seeking extension of time under Rule 138. If not filed within stipulated time, petition under Rule 137 can be filed to condone irregularity before grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of WIPO CASE participation on Section 8(2) invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the Indian Patent Office is participating in WIPO CASE as both providing and accessing office, the requirements for inviting documents under Section 8(2) have been reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect fewer invitations to file Section 8(2) documents over time as centralized access to foreign prosecution records improves, though Controllers may still request particular documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between mandatory nature of 8(1) and conditional nature of 8(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations under Section 8(1) are mandatory if there are 'same or substantially same' foreign applications being filed; obligations under Section 8(2) arise only when the Controller raises an objection and asks for such details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Form 3 disclosure (8(1)) as a mandatory duty where applicable; treat provision of prosecution documents (8(2)) as responsive to Controller's request but prudent to prepare such documents in advance.
